official_sources.verified_fact: Start-Process can return a Process object with PassThru and can redirect standard output and error to files.
official_sources.limitation: A caller must still impose a finite wait and handle termination.

official_sources.verified_fact: Wait-Process supports TimeoutSec and otherwise has no default timeout.
official_sources.limitation: Wait-Process tracks selected processes, while descendant cleanup needs a separate policy.

official_sources.verified_fact: Process.WaitForExit(Int32) waits only for the specified number of milliseconds.
official_sources.limitation: The process must be explicitly terminated if the bounded wait returns false.

official_sources.verified_fact: taskkill /PID with /T ends the selected process and child processes; /F forces termination.
official_sources.limitation: Permissions and process ownership can still prevent termination.

official_sources.verified_fact: GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT=false prevents Git from prompting on the terminal for authentication.
official_sources.limitation: Credentials must already be available or the operation fails.

official_sources.verified_fact: Git HTTP low-speed limits and time can be overridden with GIT_HTTP_LOW_SPEED_LIMIT and GIT_HTTP_LOW_SPEED_TIME.
official_sources.limitation: Values must balance slow valid transfers against stalled connections.

official_sources.verified_fact: Start-Process -Wait waits for a process tree, unlike Wait-Process which waits only for identified processes.
official_sources.limitation: This pipeline uses explicit timeout and taskkill because an unbounded -Wait can still hang.

official_sources.verified_fact: Process.Kill immediately stops the associated process; tree termination semantics depend on the overload and runtime.
official_sources.limitation: Windows PowerShell runtime compatibility makes taskkill /T the preferred tree-safe path.
